ground_truth.description: The original HashMap::collect() from an iterator silently overwrites duplicate template names — the last entry wins. This corrupts the adjacency graph used for SCC detection because the earlier template's index is lost. The fix detects duplicates explicitly and reports them as diagnostics while preserving the first entry.
The diagnostic for duplicate template names reports the indices but not the file/line where each template was defined. Adding span information would help users locate and fix the duplicates.

Duplicate detection uses get-then-insert (two hash lookups) with reviewer-facing comments ('Use explicit insertion so that duplicates are detected...', 'Keep the first entry (prev wins) — don't overwrite.') explaining the branch; HashMap::entry with Vacant/Occupied, already used for duplicate function signatures in lib.rs, expresses first-wins directly without the prose.

The only caller (compile, lib.rs:3981) receives templates already deduplicated by seen_entity_names, which emits a span-labelled 'duplicate entity definition' error and compiles only the first definition, so the new duplicate branch is unreachable from user source and duplicates an existing user-facing policy; if ever reached it would emit a second, span-less error citing internal Vec indices. The task explicitly asked for an error Diagnostic here, so the findings' debug_assert alternative contradicts the brief; the real residue is the unreachability and the uninformative message.

duplicate_template_names_emits_diagnostic only checks that some diagnostic message contains 'duplicate': it does not assert error severity (which the task's test_strategy requires), that exactly one such diagnostic is emitted, or that the name index resolves to the first template (the determinism the task asks to fix and document). Both templates are empty, so reverting to last-wins collect() plus a separate warning would still pass.

task.title: Report duplicate template names in the recursion-detection pass
task.description: `detect_recursive_structures` in `crates/reify-compiler/src/scc.rs` builds a `name -> index` map over the `TopologyTemplate` set before running Tarjan's SCC search, and a model declaring two templates under the same name is currently compiled without complaint. Make the pass surface the collision: push an error `Diagnostic` naming the duplicated template into the same `diagnostics` sink the pass already writes its cycle warnings to. Fix and document which of the colliding templates the name index resolves to, so the adjacency built from `sub_components` and the `is_recursive` tagging that follows stay deterministic regardless of template order. Observable outcome: compiling a model with two same-named templates yields a duplicate-name error diagnostic, and the recursion analysis over the rest of the model is unchanged.
task.test_strategy: Add a unit test in the `scc.rs` test module that runs `detect_recursive_structures` over two minimal templates sharing a name and asserts an error-severity diagnostic mentioning the duplicate is emitted. Keep the existing cycle-detection tests green — single-node self-edge, multi-node cycle, and the duplicate-sub-ref dedup case — so the added bookkeeping does not change cycle warnings for well-formed models. `cargo test -p reify-compiler`.
